horizon.title: (Historical) Does the --zero decomposer loop decay, or persist? — tested on 0.5.0 survivors
horizon.note: Seed panel originally 31002,31003,31014,31017. 31014 alone was re-run after a per-seed timeout that has since been fixed to scale with horizon; the full panel is now re-run so that EVERY seed carries a measured conservation residual (residualPct), not just a population trajectory. Population and B/D cannot establish conservation on their own, so the ledger residual is the quantity that matters and all four seeds must report it.
horizon.$comment: Runs LONGER than the pre-registered flatline horizon on the four surviving seeds, to distinguish an energy-POSITIVE loop (gains energy) from a neutrally stable loop (recycles the founder endowment without decay). The distinction decides whether the flatline falsification is a conservation break or a criticality result. Horizon is 4x the flatline arm.
horizon.hypothesis: Two competing readings of the flatline falsification. H-A (leak): the decomposer loop is energy-positive, so it persists AND grows with horizon. H-B (criticality): the loop conserves energy and merely recycles the founder endowment, so it persists without growing and will eventually decay as basal dissipation outpaces recycling.
horizon.prediction: H-A predicts population at 24000 ticks EXCEEDS its 6000-tick value. H-B predicts it is the same order of magnitude, oscillating, with decomp B/D near 1.0 and no upward trend across the four checkpoints.
horizon.falsification: H-A is falsified if no seed exceeds its 6000-tick population at 24000 ticks, or if decomp B/D falls below 1.0 on every seed. H-B is falsified if any seed grows monotonically beyond its 6000-tick value.
horizon.notPredicted: Absolute population values are not predicted; only the SHAPE across checkpoints distinguishes the two hypotheses.
confoundsControlled: Same four seeds that survived the flatline arm, unchanged
Same argv, same --zero preset, no lifts
Only the horizon differs from the flatline arm
One variable: ticks
horizon.status: HISTORICAL — superseded, not a live arm
horizon.horizonRelationNote: WAS 4x the flatline horizon when the flatline was registered at 6000. The flatline baseline is now 12000, so 24000 is 2x, not 4x. The original text would mislead anyone checking that ratio.
horizon.statusNote: Its four seeds (31002, 31003, 31014, 31017) were survivors of the 0.5.0 LEAKY-engine flatline. Under 0.6.0 only ONE seed (41015) was alive at tick 6000, and those four are not it. The contrast the arm was registered for has no counterpart under the corrected engine, and a green run would NOT validate it. The question is moot.
horizon.verifiedFinding: Answered: 31002/31003/31017 went extinct by tick 8000 with decomp B/D 0.99; 31014 grew monotonically to a 60000 cap. The cause was decomposer photosynthesis remaining ENABLED under --zero. Critically, that energy was BOOKED as capture in totalInput(), not omitted from it: the accounting identity balanced to 5 decimal places the whole time (residualPct 0.00000). That is exactly why a balanced residual cannot detect a bad zero baseline — the books were honest about energy that should never have entered. Fixed by P0-2 (decomposerPhotoScale added to ZEROED) and confirmed by the 0.6.0 run showing capture=0.0 and seed 31014 extinct by tick 3000.
horizon.replacement: None registered. A prospective horizon claim on the corrected engine needs a NEW seed panel registered before inspection; the only 0.6.0 near-survivor observed is 41015.

flatline.title: Flatline zero-energy regression baseline (replay on known seeds)
flatline.hypothesis: With every energy-giving pathway zeroed, all guilds go extinct. This is a REGRESSION CRITERION on a seed panel whose outcomes are already known, not a prospective ecological test: a deterministic replay of the same seeds and engine cannot confirm anything it did not already show.
flatline.prediction: REPLAY CRITERION: all 36 seeds read pop = 0 at tick 12000. A prospective ecological claim would require a NEW seed panel registered BEFORE its outcomes are inspected; that panel is not yet registered and no verdict is claimed for it.
flatline.falsification: Any of the 36 seeds reads pop > 0 at tick 12000 (would mean the correction is not deterministic, or extinction regressed).
flatline.notPredicted: Extinction TIMING within the horizon is not predicted, only terminal state. Pre-0.6.0 extinction windows are earlier-engine evidence and are not comparable.
confoundsControlled: Same 36-seed panel as every prior flatline run (41001-41018, 31001-31018)
--zero only, no lifts, so the arm remains fully specified
Declared INPUTS controlled: seeds, horizon, and every zeroed pathway identical across runs.

NOT controlled — SCHEMA AND SEMANTICS CHANGED: the knob schema is NOT unchanged between 0.4.1 and 0.6.0. decomposerPhotoScale was ADDED, the guild capture gate gained a decomposer branch, and the mineralisation return gained an nCells divisor. Declared input values were held constant; engine semantics were not.
NOT controlled: the horizon changed from 6000 to 12000. This is a re-registration, not a matched comparison, and must not be read as one.
NOT independent: outcomes at 12000 were already observed on these seeds before the horizon was set. See registrationKind.
flatline.horizonRationale: Set to 12000 AFTER observing the same seeds: latest extinction was tick 7000, so 6000 fails its own prediction on 1 of 36 seeds. 12000 gives 5000 ticks of margin. Sufficient FOR THESE 36 SEEDS; not claimed sufficient in general and not claimed independently confirmed.
flatline.measured_0_6_0: Ladder run 38110148193, engine ba0df5a: 35/36 extinct at tick 6000, 36/36 by tick 7000, 0/36 alive at 24000. Conservation under --zero across all 36 seeds: mean |residual| 0.00028%, max 0.00162%, against a 0.5% failure threshold. Verdict on the OLD 6000-tick registration: FALSIFIED (1/36 alive at 6000). The origin reference is otherwise VALID: --zero is flat and energy is conserved to five decimal places.
flatline.reRegistered: 2026-10-10, after the 0.6.0 run on the SAME 36 seeds

consumer-yield.title: Consumer viability under corrected predation assimilation
consumer-yield.$comment: Predation yield moved from cd^2 to cd in 0.5.0 (a ~25% net gain at cd~0.8). This arm asks whether that alone restores consumer viability. It is a NEW arm, not a replication of the 0.4.1 rung 6, whose lift set was never recorded.
consumer-yield.hypothesis: Removing the doubled digestion tax raises consumer net yield enough to move consumers from ~0 into persistent three-guild worlds on a majority of seeds.
consumer-yield.prediction: consumers > 0 on at least 12/18 seeds at tick 6000, AND all three guilds non-zero on at least 12/18 seeds.
consumer-yield.falsification: consumers == 0 on 7 or more of 18 seeds, or all three guilds non-zero on fewer than 12/18 seeds.

prospective-guilds.title: PROSPECTIVE replication: does the three-guild rate replicate on unseen seeds?
prospective-guilds.registrationKind: PROSPECTIVE — seed panel chosen and registered BEFORE any outcome was observed
prospective-guilds.hypothesis: The three-guild rate measured on the 41001-41018 panel (~5/18) is a property of the engine, not of that panel. Closing the decomposer capture leak removed the decomposer surplus that was propping up coexistence, so three-guild worlds should be RARE on unseen seeds too, and consumer presence should remain common.
prospective-guilds.prediction: PROSPECTIVE, stated before inspection: consumers > 0 on at least 12/18, AND all three guilds non-zero on at most 8/18. The first clause asserts consumer viability replicates; the second asserts the BALANCE shortfall replicates rather than being an artefact of the old panel.
prospective-guilds.falsification: FALSIFIED if consumers > 0 on fewer than 12/18 (consumer viability does not replicate), OR all three guilds are non-zero on 9 or more of 18 (the shortfall was panel-specific and balance is reachable once the accounting is honest).
prospective-guilds.notPredicted: Exact counts are not predicted. Consumer-yield on the old panel was 14/18 consumers and 5/18 three-guild; this arm asks whether those RATES hold, not whether they match exactly.
prospective-guilds.whyThisPanel: 52001-52018 have never been run under any arm on any engine version. The 41001-41018 panel has been inspected repeatedly across 0.4.1, 0.5.0 and 0.6.0, so it cannot support an independent claim.

graze-link.title: LINK TEST: does lifting grazeYieldScale to declared restore grazing flux?
graze-link.hypothesis: Step-0 meter (2026-10-12) showed 66-73% of graze submits resolve with positive takes that the world multiplies by the preset grazeYieldScale=0, so world flux is exactly zero by configuration. Restoring the declared scale (1.0) on the otherwise identical config should restore paying graze wins. Meat stays zeroed by design: one path at a time.
graze-link.prediction: grazeEnergy > 0 on at least 12/18 seeds at tick 6000 (read from per-seed B/D lines; the cohort verifier has no graze metric, so this arm carries no machine criteria and classifies 'not measured' by design — the verdict is human-read from intact evidence, stated here before inspection). Ecological coexistence is explicitly NOT predicted by this arm: it tests the link, not balance.
graze-link.falsification: FALSIFIED as a link restoration if grazeEnergy = 0 on 7 or more of 18 seeds. A falsification here sends the program back to contest biology (defender losses were 27-34% at Step 0), not to a larger scale — do not push to 1.6+ blindly; rung 4 already showed enriched transfer without coexistence.
graze-link.notPredicted: Endpoint guild counts, coexistence rates, and per-win sizes are not predicted. Tissue basis (plantYieldPerMass) is a follow-up only if per-win size disappoints, not part of this arm.
confoundsControlled: Same 18-seed panel, horizon, engine, and lifts as consumer-yield; the ONLY difference is +grazeYieldScale:1.0

graze-link.knownLimits: Link test only. Cohort integrity is machine-verified; the graze verdict is human-read from B/D lines and reported as observed, not as a machine classification. Says nothing about balance, viability, or decomposers.

Stepping the rain down 5x should shift the income base toward producers/grazing without killing consumers; the graze link (now paying) is what carries them through the descent.

graze-subsidy05.falsification: FALSIFIED if cons = 0 on 7 or more of 18 seeds: the cut outran the link — hold the subsidy at 0.25, do not descend further, return to link/viability work. Separately, if consumers persist but grazeEnergy = 0 on >=7/18, the descent re-silenced the link and the config is incoherent: stop, do not interpret persistence as success.

graze-viability.title: VIABILITY: breeding reserve 90 -> 30 where food demonstrably pays?
graze-viability.hypothesis: Step-3c analysis showed grazing income does not separate persisting from failing consumers (failures carry equal or greater graze energy; disease negligible; B/D<1 from the first checkpoints). The mapped gates point at the 90-tick breeding reserve against small consumer incomes. Rung 6 falsified rsur-30 in a different ecology (0.25 subsidy, uncoupled, unpaid graze); this tests the same dial where food demonstrably pays.

graze-viability.falsification: FALSIFIED if cons = 0 on 7 or more of 18 seeds: the reserve is not the binding constraint — viability needs engine-level upkeep/damage economics, and that decision goes to the Owner with this record attached. No further reserve descent (30 -> 0 would breed from nothing and break the closed budget); no compensating light or subsidy moves.
